assignment: Write an access plan for a fictional outpatient scheduling team. Use operational data only.
source: Monday morning has 12 interpreter requests and six on-site slots. Tuesday has four requests and six slots. Four Monday patients have agreed to a Tuesday appointment and two require Monday because of transport. A remote interpreter can cover two Monday slots. The team must preserve patient choice and track delays by language.

criteria.full: Shows that moving at most two patients into Tuesday's spare slots leaves ten on Monday before remote coverage, with only eight total Monday slots.
criteria.partial: Recognizes the bottleneck but overuses Tuesday or remote capacity.

criteria.full: Uses consent and transport constraints explicitly and avoids assuming all four volunteers can be moved.
criteria.partial: Mentions consent or transport but not both.

criteria.full: Proposes a concrete route for the remaining two requests, with ownership and a confirmation deadline.
criteria.partial: Identifies a residual gap without arranging additional coverage or a callback.

criteria.full: Defines a language-stratified wait or cancellation measure and a time to review it.
criteria.partial: Proposes a general satisfaction metric without a denominator or review.
